acceptance_examples: A validated repository pack is the only policy input used by a check.
A pack with a reused policy ID is rejected with the conflicting path.
An externally checkable approved claim without a source is rejected.
Duplicate IDs, bad references, selectors, levels, and missing evidence fail validation.
A check requires explicit audience, channel, funnel stage, locale, and optional campaign context.
Changing one context field changes only the matching messages and rules.
Missing must, should, and opportunity messages have distinct decision effects.
The resolved result lists every applicable policy ID and message requirement.
Checks return pass, needs_revision, or blocked without a composite score.
Each supported finding type is produced by its matching configured policy.
A triggered finding includes policy ID, severity, certainty, rationale, evidence, and location.
Suggestions repair a bounded message and never replace the submitted draft.
Repeated deterministic checks produce deeply equal, stably sorted results.
Confirmed and model-assisted findings expose different certainty labels.
With no semantic adapter, deterministic checks run and semantic status is not_run.
A semantic contradiction remains model_assisted, warns, and needs human review.
Only a matching deterministic contradiction rule creates a confirmed contradiction.
A competitive claim without active approval, named competitor, qualifier, and evidence is flagged.
A prohibited competitor claim with block enforcement returns a confirmed blocking finding.
A campaign resolves its narrative, action, requirements, avoid list, and proof references.
Campaign requirements narrow company policy without approving a prohibited company claim.
Architecture policy proves the domain and application layers have no MCP, model, network, or HYV dependency.
CLI init, validate, check, and serve commands expose their documented contracts.
All MCP tools publish structured schemas and read-only closed-world annotations.
MCP lists and executes context, brief, check, and explanation tools.
CLI JSON and MCP structured output equal the shared service result for one input.
A spawned stdio server completes an MCP handshake without protocol text on stderr.
Default execution completes offline and leaves no submitted draft artifact.
The process loads only the explicitly configured pack path.
Oversized packs, files, and stdin fail with the configured byte limit.
Instruction-like draft text is evaluated only as literal data signals.
Every public MCP tool is read-only and no CLI command mutates policy except explicit init.
The repository documentation check confirms all required OSS files and local links.
The CI definition runs format, lint, type, unit, integration, package, and dependency checks.
A clean tarball install on a supported Node version exposes only expected release files and a working binary.
A new user can follow the documented CLI and local MCP quick starts without unpublished services.
